bugs.error_message: MFC vertical F_k and command blow up to +/-infinity on the ground after bug-030 fix
bugs.root_cause: The MFC algebraic estimator is effectively an integrator: cmd[k] ~= cmd[k-1] + (ydd_ref - kp^2*err)/alpha. On the ground z_meas==0 while the altitude reference ramps, so err never decays -> integrator windup -> F_k diverges. mfc_siso_run accepts in_flight but ignores it (mfc_core.c:95). The stabilizer avoids this because attitude error ~0 (plant responds); vertical guidance on the ground does not.
bugs.fix: Gate the estimator on in_flight in guidance_mfc_vert: while !in_flight, re-latch the clock (keeps mfc.time < 0.1 gate), zero cmd history, and output GUIDANCE_MFC_GZ_NOMINAL_HOVER_THROTTLE; run MFC only in flight (fresh start at takeoff). v_thrust.z now steady 0.30 on ground.
bugs.resolution_note: SUPERSEDED by bug-033 (2026-06-11). The in_flight ground-gating + per-cycle clock re-latch was removed; guidance_mfc_vert() now runs raw MFC every cycle whenever gz is enabled. Ground windup protection intentionally dropped per user request.

bugs.error_message: Vehicle won't take off with clean 0.30 MFC throttle; in_flight never trips
bugs.root_cause: User edit `v_thrust.z = thrust->sp.thrust_f[THRUST_AXIS_Z]` feeds a normalised throttle (0.30) into the WLS thrust objective indi_v[3], which lives in PPRZ*effectiveness units. Stock mapping: th_cmd.z=0.30*9600=2880, Bwls[3][i]=g1_thrust/INDI_G_SCALING=-1.5/1000=-0.0015, hover objective = sum 2880*(-0.0015) ~= -17.3. So indi_v[3] needs ~-17.3; edit feeds +0.30 (~58x too small AND wrong sign) -> WLS commands motors ~off -> no takeoff -> in_flight never set. Not newtons; nothing converts to force.
bugs.fix: DIAGNOSED ONLY (user's intentional edit, not reverted). Options: (1) revert to stock v_thrust.z += th_cmd.z*Bwls[3][i]*act_thrust_mat[2][i] [recommended]; or (2) make guidance output the indi_v[3]-space value (~-17 at hover) and retune GZ_ALPHA + sign. Awaiting user choice.
bugs.resolution_note: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (user-confirmed: MFC Z guidance flies perfectly smooth in NPS). The absolute-thrust edit (stabilization_indi.c:741 v_thrust.z = thrust_f) was RETAINED, i.e. option (2) from the diagnosis: guidance outputs an indi_v[3]-space thrust and GZ was retuned so it enters the WLS objective at the correct scale. Not reverted to stock.

bugs.error_message: PlotJuggler UDP JSON Server crashes/stops streaming: [json.exception.parse_error.101] ... invalid string: forbidden character after backslash; last read: '"PPRZ\p'  AND  ... invalid literal; last read: '"innov_vel": na'. Much worse with a real telemetry radio than in sim.
bugs.root_cause: server.ml's UDP JSON emitter (json_of_message in vendored pprzlink) has two bugs: (1) String field values are spliced into the JSON with zero escaping (`sprintf "\"%s\": \"%s\"" field_name s`) -- any backslash/quote/control byte in the field breaks the JSON outright. Real RF telemetry corrupts raw bytes far more often than the sim's loopback link, so this shows up much worse on real hardware. (2) Float fields use plain `%f`; OCaml's %f renders NaN/Inf as the bare identifiers nan/inf/-inf, which are not valid JSON literals (nlohmann's parser aborts, reporting the truncated 'na' context). NaN innov_vel is common on real hardware when the EKF hasn't converged.
bugs.fix: Did not patch vendored pprzlink (used elsewhere, would need a rebuild). Instead added pj_json_relay.py at the repo root: a UDP relay/sanitizer that sits between server.ml and PlotJuggler (also replaces the socat hop already needed to bridge the VM interface to localhost:9870). It passes valid JSON through untouched, repairs the two known bug patterns (escapes stray backslashes/control bytes inside strings, replaces bare nan/-nan/inf/-inf with null) via a single-pass tokenizer, and drops+logs anything still unparseable so PlotJuggler never sees invalid JSON. Verified against both exact repro strings from the user's error messages plus a live UDP send/receive smoke test.

bugs.error_message: Wrong reference: header should be file
HEOL gz mode entry commanded ~2x hover thrust on the first tick
bugs.root_cause: guidance_v_run_enter() pre-seeded heol_gz.mfc.command[0..1] to the nominal hover thrust, copied from guidance_mfc's gz entry. In guidance_mfc mfc.command[0] IS the total thrust command; in HEOL it is only the correction u_fb, so the total came out u_ff + hover. It also fed the estimator's delayed-command term a value that was never a correction, and GZ_COMMAND_FILTER=8 stretched the transient over several ticks.
bugs.fix: Removed the pre-seed. heol_reset() already zeroes the command history, which is the correct HEOL seed (enter with no correction, so the first tick commands exactly the feedforward). Added a comment warning not to reintroduce it.

bugs.error_message: HEOL total thrust command unbounded above; saturation applied to the wrong quantity
bugs.root_cause: mfc_core clamped only the correction du against a window pre-offset by a CONSTANT hover u_ff, then heol.c added u_ff afterwards with no further clamp. Valid only while u_ff was constant; FLAT_TRAJ_DEMO_ORDER=4 made u_ff time-varying, so the fixed offset no longer bounded the sum. The symmetric window also admitted physically impossible positive total thrust.
bugs.fix: Added u_min/u_max on HeolParameters expressing the TOTAL command's physical range ([-GZ_MAX_THRUST, 0] for gz). heol_run() shifts that window into u_fb's frame each tick (mfc.u_min = u_min - u_ff), which is algebraically the same clamp but keeps it inside mfc_siso_run() where the anti-windup freeze observes it in the same sample. Degenerate inverted window collapses onto the reachable edge. GCS u_min/u_max settings re-pointed to the new HEOL-level fields.

bugs.error_message: Vertical HEOL loop diverges when alpha_z is scheduled from the true Jacobian
bugs.root_cause: alpha_z = cos(theta*)cos(phi*)/m runs 1.01-1.25 vs the constant GZ_ALPHA=6.25, so alpha drops ~5x and enters inverted. NOT a loop-gain problem: a constant alpha error is self-cancelling in the decoupled iPD law because the estimator absorbs it into F_hat, leaving the closed-loop polynomial s^2+kd*s+kp unchanged. What a 5x smaller alpha actually does is amplify ESTIMATOR error 5x, since -F_hat/alpha dominates -fb/alpha.
bugs.fix: Landed as a selectable flag (guidance_heol_gz_alpha_from_jacobian / GZ_ALPHA_FROM_JACOBIAN), defaulting to the spec's Jacobian, after the author confirmed the gain mismatch is not a blocker on an untuned new controller. Tuning debt is documented at the call site: PD rescaling does NOT recover it (constant alpha error is self-cancelling via F_hat), so the lever is int_window/est_hold_time. SITL with JACOBIAN: RMS 0.58 m vs 0.059 m with CONST.

bugs.error_message: NPS_SENSORS_PARAMS silently ignored in nps_sensor_accel.c and nps_sensors.c: 'noise off' left the accelerometer at full stock noise
bugs.root_cause: nps_sensors.h picks the sensor-parameter file with `#ifndef NPS_SENSORS_PARAMS`, and NPS_SENSORS_PARAMS is an airframe define living in generated/airframe.h. Those two TUs included nps_sensors.h WITHOUT including generated/airframe.h first, so they took the #ifndef branch (nps_sensors_params_default.h) while nps_sensor_gyro/mag/gps/baro/sonar.c (which do include airframe.h first) took the #else branch. Different noise parameters in different translation units of the same binary. Latent upstream bug: affects any airframe that sets NPS_SENSORS_PARAMS.
bugs.fix: Added `#include "generated/airframe.h"` before `#include "nps_sensors.h"` in both files, matching the sibling sensor TUs. Verified by preprocessing: before, accel resolved to nps_sensors_params_default.h and gyro to nps_sensors_params_anton_mfc.h; after, all three resolve to the anton header. Confirmed in flight: accelerometer first-difference std drops 31.77 -> 0.26 between NOISE_SCALE 1 and 0.

bugs.error_message: Two NPS sim runs streamed into one capture CSV; analysis reported a physically impossible flight (|phi| pinned at 3.14 rad while agl held 2.1 m)
bugs.file: sim_anton.py / sim.sh (usage pattern, not a code defect)
bugs.root_cause: sim.sh/sim_anton.py never self-terminate; `timeout -s INT` leaves the capture relay alive on 127.0.0.1:9871. A second sim started while the first relay still listens is ingested into the FIRST run's CSV. Compounded by attributing the log with `ls -t` instead of the filename the run printed.
bugs.fix: Serialize runs: `docker rm -f` + settle before and after each sim, and take the CSV name from that run's own stdout. Added a checker that flags contamination from row rate (~500/s expected), duplicate timestamps and backward time steps; two contaminated captures were caught and re-run.

bugs.error_message: GCS sliders for guidance command_filter could not represent the flown value (GZ_COMMAND_FILTER = 8) and allowed a divide hazard
bugs.root_cause: gx/gy/gz_cfilt dl_settings were min="0." max="1.", but command_filter is a divisor where 1 = no smoothing and larger = more. The flown GZ value of 8 is outside the slider range, so touching the slider would silently disable the filter; min=0 is a division hazard.
bugs.fix: Changed all three to min="1." step="1." max="50.", matching the stabilization_mfc.xml panel.

bugs.error_message: MFC estimator was fed the PRE-saturation command on all six axes; limit-cycle generator on any saturating axis
bugs.root_cause: mfc_siso_init set est_use_presat_command = true. The upstream Simulink mfc_siso.step ends `state.u_km1 = u` with u post-EMA and post-clamp. Feeding the pre-saturation model-inversion output makes F_hat attribute to the plant a command it never received; when the clamp bites F_hat drifts to cover the difference and drives the command further into the rail. Nothing in stabilization_mfc.c or guidance_mfc.c overrode the default, so all six axes ran it.
bugs.fix: Default flipped to false (tap the applied, post-clamp command). Same defect had been diagnosed independently on HEOL, which is why guidance_heol.c already exposed a per-axis knob.

bugs.error_message: Vertical loop limit-cycled between both thrust clamps (10-30 m excursions on a 3 m setpoint) after 'improving' the gz channel
bugs.root_cause: Three separate well-intentioned changes each broke it: (1) GZ_INTEGRATION_WINDOW 4->50 -- in the COUPLED structure int_window is the estimator bandwidth and the estimator IS the feedback path, so this detuned the controller 12x; (2) switching gz to DECOUPLED with Simulink's Kd/windows simultaneously; (3) adding the x/y 3 Hz Butterworth to the z measurement -- ~60 ms lag into a channel whose ref filter and estimator window are both 8 ms.
bugs.fix: All three reverted; gz left on its native fast coupled config with the raw z measurement. Result: err_z rms 1.7 mm, cmd_z smooth with no clamping. guidance_mfc.c now documents why z is unfiltered. Rule: check coupled vs decoupled before reasoning about a window, and compare any new filter's lag against the axis's windows in milliseconds.

bugs.error_message: Flat trajectory: vehicle climbs ~1.7 m past the endpoint and holds there; cmd_z slams between +7.848 N clamp and -18 N at 10 Hz; MFC_GUIDANCE/sp_z visibly hatched instead of a flat line
bugs.root_cause: gv_update_ref_from_flat_ref() round-tripped gv_z_ref (Q37.26) through INT32_POS_FRAC (Q23.8) every tick, discarding 18 fractional bits. BFP_OF_REAL truncates toward zero and NED altitude is negative, so the truncation moved the reference UP a whole LSB (3.9 mm) per 2 ms tick regardless of the true step size -- a ratchet, = +1.95 m/s phantom climb. gv_set_flat_ref() re-synced at the slower nav rate, making z_ref a ~10 Hz sawtooth. Invisible to a PID, but MFC/HEOL double-differentiate the setpoint (dot_dot_setpoint_trajec), so each snap-back was an rddot impulse ~1e4 m/s^2 that pinned the thrust command at its clamp.
bugs.fix: Accumulate the position STEP at gv_z_ref's native Q37.26 resolution (llroundf) instead of round-tripping the absolute value; round rather than truncate the speed/accel write-backs. A float cannot hold the absolute value at Q37.26 (3 m * 2^26 = 2e8 > 24-bit mantissa), so converting the small step is the correct form. Verified by a standalone harness reproducing +1.95 m/s from the old arithmetic (matching the flight log to 3 s.f.) and ~1e-7 m error from the new; then confirmed in flight.

bugs.error_message: Flat trajectory run from the GCS reverts to a Standby-like hold on its own; GCS shows only a momentary flicker to GUIDED
bugs.root_cause: autopilot_static_on_rc_frame() re-derives the autopilot mode from the RC 3-way switch every RC frame, so autopilot_set_mode(AP_MODE_GUIDED) from the flight plan survived one frame before being stamped back to AP_MODE_NAV (AUTO2). The block kept running and kept calling guidance_h_set_flat(), but guidance_h.mode was GUIDANCE_H_MODE_NAV again, so guidance_h_from_nav() served the setpoint from nav.carrot -- the previous block's leftover waypoint (Standby's). No RC link exists in SITL, so it reproduced only from the GCS.
bugs.fix: Stay in AP_MODE_NAV; set nav.horizontal_mode = NAV_HORIZONTAL_MODE_GUIDED and nav.vertical_mode = NAV_VERTICAL_MODE_GUIDED every tick in nav_flat_traj_run(). These are NAV sub-mode selectors, not autopilot modes, so the RC switch cannot touch them, and they dispatch to the same guided runners. Mirrors the stock NavGuided() macro. Removed autopilot_set_mode(AP_MODE_GUIDED) from the flight plan.

bugs.error_message: DARKO_FINDI diverged 178 m in SITL on the first flight; pitch drifted to +69 deg while zeta_e stayed ~0
bugs.root_cause: NOT a port bug. The airframe simulates JSBSim 'cyclone', which is not DarkO: its wing makes 0.74 N of lift at 5 m/s against the DarkO model's 8.96 N (12x). The flatness force transform is an open-loop aerodynamic inversion, so it hands most of the weight to a wing that is not there and commands 62 deg of tilt at 5 m/s; speed then grows -> more tilt -> positive feedback. zeta_e ~ 0 during the departure was the tell: the aircraft was TRACKING a bad command, not failing to track a good one. Reproduces with every NPS noise source zeroed, so it is structural.
bugs.fix: Promoted GUIDANCE_FINDI_DARKO_TRANSFORM_V_SCALE (module default 1.0 = the published law); at 0 the transform reduces to pure thrust vectoring and the aircraft hovers to 0.098 m rms. Real fix is a JSBSim model matching flatness_darko.h's measured constants; until that exists no SITL result speaks to the aerodynamic half of the inversion.

bugs.error_message: heol_mimo.c / oneloop_fmfc_darko_law.h: the `lo > hi` collapse branch in the clamp-window computation is unreachable, and its comment misdescribes what it guards
bugs.root_cause: lo = u_min - u_ff and hi = u_max - u_ff, so `lo > hi` reduces to `u_min > u_max` -- it does NOT detect 'u_ff is already outside [u_min, u_max]', which is what the comment claims. A u_ff outside the bounds simply produces a shifted window that correctly forces the correction to pull it back in. Found by a property check written against the comment, which failed.
bugs.fix: Kept the branch as a guard against a caller that inverts its own bounds, corrected the comment in oneloop_fmfc_darko_law.h to say so, and replaced the harness check with one that asserts the real property: the window is never inverted, it forces the correction in the right direction, and the total lands on the reachable edge. heol_mimo.c itself was NOT edited (a flying controller, and the branch is harmless).

bugs.error_message: DARKO_FMFC in SITL: arms and holds altitude but the horizontal channel is saturated on the 30 deg tilt limiter 100% of the settled window; position residual sits at 12-16 m rms and never captures the waypoint. With noise on, two of three runs departed and landed within 20-40 s.
bugs.root_cause: NOT diagnosed to a port bug -- 109 structural property checks pass, including the tsPD identity against findi_darko_tspd(). Reproduces with every NPS noise source zeroed, so it is structural, not noise. Peak pitch attitude error 1.3 rad (75 deg) says the inner loop cannot follow the attitude the transform commands. Two live suspects, both flagged not fixed: (a) the inner gains are UNTUNED placeholders (4, 6) = wn 2 zeta 1.5, against findi_darko's MEASURED (25, 7.0) = wn 5 zeta 0.7; (b) an MFC bracket does not integrate on the command, so the 2.2x cyclone/DarkO mass mismatch that findi_darko's increment cancelled is instead CARRIED in F_hat (observed F_hat_lin_z 0.6-3.1 m/s^2).
bugs.fix: NOT FIXED, deliberately. The brief is integration-only: report, do not tune. Two in-flight A/Bs to (25, 7.0) via --set both went inverted within ~5 s, but both applied the change during a transient so neither is a clean comparison -- the flagged gain is a suspect, not a demonstrated fix. Next step is the attitude-only rung (fmfc_darko_linear_enabled = false, driven with --rc_script 0), and the Simulink side tuning first.
